interface.name: kywc_toplevel_manager_v1
interface.description:
A toplevel is defined as a surface with a role similar to xdg_toplevel. XWayland surfaces may be treated like toplevels in this protocol.
After a client binds the global, each mapped toplevel window will be sent using the toplevel event.

event.name: toplevel
event.description:
This event is emitted whenever a new toplevel window is created. It is emitted for all toplevels, regardless of the app that has created them.
All initial properties of the toplevel (identifier, title, app_id) will be sent immediately after this event using the corresponding events for kywc_toplevel. The compositor will use the done event to indicate when all data has been sent.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor has finished with the toplevel manager

event.description:
This event indicates that the compositor is done sending events to this object. The client should destroy the object. See destroy for more information.
The compositor must not send any more toplevel events after this event.

request.name: stop
request.description:
This request indicates that the client no longer wishes to receive events for new toplevels.
The Wayland protocol is asynchronous, meaning the compositor may send further toplevel events until the stop request is processed. The client should wait for a finished event before destroying this object.

interface.name: kywc_toplevel_v1
interface.description: A kywc_toplevel_v1 object represents a mapped toplevel window. A single app may have multiple mapped toplevels.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request should be used when the client will no longer use the toplevel or after the closed event has been received to allow destruction of the object.

event.name: closed
event.description: The server will emit no further events on the kywc_toplevel_v1 after this event. Any requests received aside from the destroy request must be ignored. Upon receiving this event, the client should destroy the handle.

event.name: done

description.summary: all information about the toplevel has been sent

event.description: This event is sent after all changes in the toplevel state have been sent.

event.name: title
event.description: The title of the toplevel has changed.

event.name: app_id
event.description: The app id of the topleve.done for details.

event.name: primary_output
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the output that the largest area of this toplevel is displayed on has changed.

event.name: workspace_enter
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the toplevel becomes visible on the given workspace. A toplevel may be visible on multiple workspaces.

event.name: workspace_leave
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the toplevel stops being visible on the given workspace. It is guaranteed that an entered-workspace event with the same workspace has been emitted before this event.

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Describes what capabilities this toplevel has.

entry.name: skip_taskbar
entry.summary: if this toplevel not be listed in the taskbar

entry.name: skip_switcher
entry.summary: if this toplevel not appear in a switcher

event.name: capabilities
event.description: What capabilities this toplevel has, sent on startup before the first done event.

enum.name: state

description.summary: types of states on the toplevel

enum.description: The different states that a toplevel can have.

event.name: state
event.description: This event is emitted immediately after the kywc_toplevel_v1 is created and each time the toplevel state changes, either because of a compositor action or because of a request in this protocol.

event.name: parent
event.description:
This event is emitted whenever the parent of the toplevel changes.
No event is emitted when the parent handle is destroyed by the client.

event.name: icon
event.description: This event will be sent whenever the icon changes. May be null.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: The geometry of this toplevel in absolute coordinates

event.description: This event will be sent whenever the toplevel geometry changes.

request.name: set_maximized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be maximized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be maximized. If the maximized state actually changes, this will be indicated by the state event.

request.name: unset_maximized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be unmaximized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be unmaximized. If the maximized state actually changes, this will be indicated by the state event.

request.name: set_minimized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be minimized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be minimized. If the minimized state actually changes, this will be indicated by the state event.

request.name: unset_minimized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be unminimized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be unminimized. If the minimized state actually changes, this will be indicated by the state event.

request.name: set_fullscreen

description.summary: request that the toplevel be fullscreened

request.description:
Requests that the toplevel be fullscreened on the given output. If the fullscreen state and/or the outputs the toplevel is visible on actually change, this will be indicated by the state and output_enter/leave events.
The output parameter is only a hint to the compositor. Also, if output is NULL, the compositor should decide which output the toplevel will be fullscreened on, if at all.

request.name: unset_fullscreen

description.summary: request that the toplevel be unfullscreened

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be unfullscreened. If the fullscreen state actually changes, this will be indicated by the state event.

request.name: activate
request.description: Request that this toplevel be activated. There is no guarantee the toplevel will be actually activated.

request.name: close

description.summary: request that the toplevel be closed

request.description: Send a request to the toplevel to close itself. The compositor would typically use a shell-specific method to carry out this request, for example by sending the xdg_toplevel.close event. However, this gives no guarantees the toplevel will actually be destroyed. If and when this happens, the closed event will be emitted.

request.name: enter_workspace
request.description: Make the toplevel enter a workspace. A toplevel can enter more than one workspace. if the id is empty or invalid, no action will be performed.

request.name: leave_workspace

description.summary: remove a toplevel from a workspace

request.description: Make the toplevel exit a workspace.

request.name: move_to_workspace
request.description: Requests this toplevel to be displayed only in a specific workspace.

request.name: move_to_output
request.description: Requests this toplevel to be displayed in a specific output.

request.name: set_position
request.description: Move the window to new coordinates.

request.name: set_size
request.description:
Set the window to new size.
Window size will be consider compositor window size limits.

event.name: pid

description.summary: process id of application owning the window

event.description: This event will only be emitted once, before the first "done" event occurs.
